name: result_publish
capability: Yuzuno can show an interactive table, chart, short form or task status proposal. When comparing options, presenting data, collecting related answers or proposing a task status for the user to confirm, use the yuzuno result_publish tool (load it with tool search if needed; result_guide has each component's full guide), fix any problems it returns, and do not repeat an accepted result in your reply. For simple questions, confirmations, or when the user asks for text only, reply in plain text.
description:
Show an interactive result (tables, charts, metrics, a short clarification form or a proposed task status change) to the user in this Turn. This is a summary: every component's exact props, limits and rules are in result_guide. Read it before your first result in a session (pass components to read only some); a rejection names it too.
Optional: use it only when structure helps — comparing options, tabular or numeric data, or collecting several related answers. For simple facts, confirmations and short answers, reply in plain text and do not call result_publish.
Pass expectedTurnId: the yuzuno.activeTurnId that peers_list returns to you during this Turn. Core checks the result before it is shown. An accepted result is displayed at the end of this Turn, below your reply: do not repeat it, its JSON or a yuzuno-ui block in your reply. A rejection lists problems as {code, path, reason}: fix them and call again with a new requestId; after 3 rejections in a Turn, answer in text. If the tool is unavailable or the Turn has changed, answer in text.
At most 3 results per Turn. To change one, pass revisesResultId: the resultId of its latest version from this Turn (at most 5 versions).
spec is {root, elements}: elements maps ids (1-64 characters: a letter, then letters, digits, - or _; every other id has the same form) to {type, props, children?}. root names a Result. The elements form one tree, at most 6 levels and 32 components, every element used, at most 64000 bytes as compact JSON. Components: Clarification, Result, Section, Text, Metrics, Table, BarChart, Sources, Continue, TaskStatus. At most one Continue, Clarification or TaskStatus; a form never approves an action or permission, and a TaskStatus changes its task only when the user confirms it.

components.text: - Clarification {id, title≤160, description?≤1000, fields[1-8]{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="text", placeholder?≤160, default?{value≤2000, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="single", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="multi", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value[≤12](string), source≤160}}}: One bounded form: id, title, optional description and 1-8 fields. Each field has id, type (text/single/multi), label, required and optional description. Text may have placeholder. Choices have 2-12 options with stable id, label and optional description. An optional default is {value, source}: source says where it came from; value is text, one option id or an array of option ids. Users explicitly submit answers once to this original conversation; never use forms as native permission approval.
- Result {title≤160, summary≤2000}: One result root with title and conclusion. Has children.
- Section {title≤160}: A titled group. Has children.
- Metrics {items[1-6]{label≤160, value≤160, detail?≤2000}}: Up to six reported metrics.

- Table {id, title?≤160, columns[1-8]{key, label≤160}, rows[≤100]{id, cells{<key>: string≤500|number|boolean|null}, sourceIds?[≤12](string)}, selectable?}: A searchable sortable table. Rows may be selected for a follow-up draft. (title defaults to "Table")
- BarChart {id, title?≤160, unit≤30, data[1-24]{id, label≤160, value, sourceIds?[≤12](string)}}: A bar chart with equivalent selectable data table. (title defaults to "Chart")
- Sources {items[≤30]{id, label≤160, href≤2000}}: Explicit HTTPS or local file references.
- Continue {label≤160, instruction≤2000, requiresSelection?}: A user-clicked button that appends instruction and current selection to a draft.

- TaskStatus {taskId, status="todo"|"doing"|"blocked"|"review"|"done"|"cancelled", reason≤1000}: Proposes one status change to one existing shared task: taskId T-N, status todo/doing/blocked/review/done/cancelled, and why. The user sees the task as Core reads it, may change the status or reason, and confirms or declines; only a confirmation changes the task, as the user.

guide.rules:
Clarification is available through result_publish, not a reply's JSON block. Keep ordinary text answers available. Required does not imply a default; include default.source whenever suggesting or pre-filling a value. Answers use original resultId/formId/field IDs and option IDs. A revision replaces the previous form and its draft stays separate. Publishing a form does not authorize any action or permission request.
A result has at most one Continue, Clarification or TaskStatus. Every Table row has a cell for each column key and no others.
TaskStatus is available through result_publish, not a reply's JSON block. Its task must exist and have another status; read it with task_get. Publishing changes nothing: the user confirms or declines, and may change the status or reason first. Propose a change only when asked to or when your work calls for one; never propose done for work you have not finished.
Sources hrefs are http(s) URLs or local file paths (optionally :line); rows and bars cite them by id in sourceIds. Table and BarChart ids, row ids and column keys are unique.

guideTool.name: result_guide
guideTool.description: The full guide to result_publish: how to publish, every component's exact props and limits, and the rules a result must follow, from the contract Core checks results with. Read-only. Call it before your first result in a session, or when a rejection names it. Pass components to read only some.

components.description: Only these components, with the usage and rules. Omit for the whole guide.

brief.hardRules:
Yuzuno Project Brief rules:
1. No Brief update is required each turn: write when something changed, for the user: conclusion first, limits beside it, evidence on its Task. A current state goes in a status, a lasting finding or decision in a short report linked to its Task, a choice for the user in an ask; result_publish never reaches Home. Load tools with tool search if needed.
2. Pass expectedVersion from brief_get. On version_conflict, re-read (the rejection has the latest), merge and retry with a new requestId.
3. Only the user selects Home content editors. If editContent is false and writeOwnAsk is true, write only your own Asks. If writeOwnAsk is false, this Brief is read-only. Editors still edit only their own sections; add a topic/sub to another author's topic.
4. An ask needs a question plus reply options, freeText, a form or a choice. A reply marks it replied. Resolve your asks explicitly with resolve once they are handled: a preference once taken in, an authorized action only after it is done and its result is on the Task or Brief. A reply executes nothing itself: act on what the user authorized, a reply included, and infer no retry, merge or permission it does not grant.
5. Brief content never executes actions: nothing you write merges, deploys or approves; answers come back to you as messages.
6. If brief_update is rejected, fix the listed problems and call it again. Read yuzuno_guide brief for what to write and brief_guide for formats, limits and examples.
brief.outcomeHint: Home: a lasting finding, decision or stage result goes in a short report linked to its Task and sources; a current state in a status; a choice for the user in an ask. result_publish shows only in this turn. How to write it: yuzuno_guide brief.

toolDescriptions.brief_get: Read your Project's Brief: its version, the live sections (key, kind, title, owner, body, ask state, status, attachments), you {agentId, ownsKeys, openAsks, repliedAsks (your asks the user answered, to act on and resolve), staleStatus, capabilities; for a Home content editor homeHint, and homePreference once the user set one: how they like results presented, current as of this read, granting nothing} and the limits. keys: omit for every section with its body; [] for an index of the sections without bodies; [key, ...] for those sections in full. Pass its version to brief_update as expectedVersion. projectId defaults to your own Project. Nothing requires reading or updating the Brief each turn. Formats: brief_guide.
toolDescriptions.brief_update: Write Brief changes when something changed; nothing requires a call each turn. Ask-only members may write only their own Asks. Pass expectedVersion (from brief_get) and a new requestId (reuse it only to retry the same call). Send changes:[...] (noChange:true changes nothing). Changes: put {op:"put", key, kind, title, body, ask?, status?, time?, attachments?} creates or replaces a section you own; edit {op:"edit", key, elements:{<id>: block}} replaces only those blocks; resolve {op:"resolve", key} resolves your ask; remove {op:"remove", key} removes your section; claim {op:"claim", key} takes an orphaned section of your Project (change it in a later call). key is topic or topic/sub (a-z, 0-9, -); add to another Agent's section with a topic/sub key of your own. kind ask needs ask {question, reply} with reply options, freeText, form or choice; kind status needs status {asOf, validFor}. body is {root, elements} with a BriefBody root. A rejection lists problems {code, path, reason, guide}: fix them and retry with a new requestId; on version_conflict merge with the latest it returns. validateOnly:true pre-checks without writing. Content never executes actions. Formats: brief_guide.
toolDescriptions.brief_guide: The Project Brief format guide, generated from the contract: sections and their kinds, ask replies, body components with props and limits, charts, attachments, error codes and worked examples; what to write is in yuzuno_guide brief. part is one of sections, ask, content, charts, attachments, limits, errors, examples; omit it for everything. Read the part a rejection's guide names: "brief_guide charts" means part charts.

brief.guide:
# brief_guide (Project Brief schema 1)

Parts: sections, ask, content, charts, attachments, limits, errors, examples. Call brief_guide with part to read one.

## sections
This guide is the format. What to write and in which form is yuzuno_guide topic brief ("Write for Home"): one conclusion first, important limits beside it, each fact in one place, and execution evidence (logs, raw data, full test output, run and PR lists) left on its Task and linked.
What goes where: Home: a lasting finding, decision or stage result goes in a short report linked to its Task and sources; a current state in a status; a choice for the user in an ask. result_publish shows only in this turn. How to write it: yuzuno_guide brief. Update a section when something changed, not every turn; a status past its validFor shows as stale until new facts refresh it. Details stay on the Task and its sources.
Home content editors are set by the user per Project. brief_get returns you.capabilities. When editContent is false and writeOwnAsk is true, only create/update/resolve/remove your own Asks or send noChange; do not claim sections, convert regular content into an Ask, or write reports/status. When writeOwnAsk is false, this Brief is read-only, including no noChange writes. Ownership rules still apply to editors. Hidden old content remains in team details/history.
brief_update takes changes: [...]. put creates or replaces one section you own:
- put {op:"put", key, kind: ask|report|status, title, body{…}, ask?{…}, status?{…}, time?{…}, attachments?[≤12]{…}}
- key: topic or topic/sub; each part 1-48 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit (round-12, round-12/review). A Brief has at most 12 topics with 4 subs each.
- kind: ask (a question for the user, see ask); report (a result the user reads and marks seen; seen reports stay in history 30 days); status (current state; needs status {asOf, validFor}, validFor 60-31536000 seconds; greyed once asOf + validFor has passed).
- title: 1-120 characters. body: {root, elements}, see content. time: due, eta and nextUpdate, ISO 8601 with a time zone. attachments: see attachments.
edit {op:"edit", key, elements:{<id>: {type, props, children?}}, status?} replaces blocks of a section you own by id and keeps the rest as it was: the other blocks and their order, title, attachments, time and the ask's state. Each id is one the body already has, or a new block named as a child by a block you edit; the root is not edited (rearrange with put). Core checks the whole section again. status (kind status only) refreshes asOf. Day to day, edit the blocks that changed, e.g. {op:"edit", key:"overview", elements:{progress:{type:"Plan", props:{steps:[...]}}}}; put a section to create it or change its layout.
Other changes: {op:"resolve", key} resolves your ask; {op:"remove", key} removes your section (reports and status go to history); {op:"claim", key} takes an orphaned section of your Project; change it in a later brief_update, not in the one that claims it.
Only a section's owner changes it. To add to another Agent's section, put your own section under its key as topic/sub; Home shows them together with each author.
Pass expectedVersion from brief_get. On version_conflict the rejection includes latest: merge and retry with a new requestId. Nothing requires an update each turn; noChange:true is still accepted and changes nothing.
validateOnly:true pre-checks a brief_update: it runs the checks made before the write, with their problems as the update would give them (and latest), and writes nothing: no requestId kept, no version or space reserved, and it is not your update. Its answer has valid, whether the pre-check passed, and checkedAll, only whether it ran all its steps. Checking stops at the first step with problems, so false means later steps did not run and the problems listed may not be all. Checks made only on writing are outside it: sending the update checks version, Turn and permissions again against the Brief as it is then, and can still be refused, e.g. with snapshot_limit when the Brief's snapshots would exceed their total. Use it for a complex section; an ordinary edit needs no check first.

## ask
kind ask needs ask:
- ask {question, reply{options?[2-8]{id, label}, freeText?: true|{prompt?}, form?{…}, choice?{a{id, label, detail?}, b{id, label, detail?}}}}: a question and how the user can answer.
- question: 1-500 characters. reply needs at least one of options, freeText, form or choice; otherwise the change is rejected.
- options: 2-8 buttons; each sends one prefilled reply message to you. freeText: true, or {prompt} to label the text box. choice: two approaches a and b.
- form {id, title≤160, description?≤1000, fields[1-8]{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="text", placeholder?≤160, default?{value≤2000, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="single", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="multi", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value[≤12](string), source≤160}}}: One bounded form: id, title, optional description and 1-8 fields. Each field has id, type (text/single/multi), label, required and optional description. Text may have placeholder. Choices have 2-12 options with stable id, label and optional description. An optional default is {value, source}: source says where it came from; value is text, one option id or an array of option ids. Users explicitly submit answers once to this original conversation; never use forms as native permission approval. At most 8 fields, 12 options each.
Use options for one choice and a form for several related answers, as in the decision and form examples.
The user's answer reaches you as an ordinary message quoting the section. The ask then shows "replied": it leaves Needs you, and brief_get lists it in you.repliedAsks (key, title, repliedAt, the reply in short, updatedSinceReply). It stays until you resolve it with {op:"resolve", key}; nothing closes it for you.
When to resolve: a preference or information you asked for, once you have taken it in; an action the reply authorizes, only after that action is confirmed done and its result is on the existing Task or a Brief section. A green CI or a whole Task being done is not that action. While it runs, or after it fails, keep the ask replied and report progress on the Task or Brief: edit keeps it replied, while put asks it again. Ask again only when the user has something new to decide. A reply executes nothing by itself: act on what the user has authorized, an explicit reply included, without asking for it again, and never infer a retry, merge or wider permission from an answer that does not grant it.
openAsks counts your unresolved asks, open or replied; at most 3 per Agent.
Answers never execute actions: nothing in a Brief merges, deploys or approves; Core approvals stay separate.

## content
body is {root, elements}: elements maps ids (a letter, then letters, digits, - or _) to {type, props, children?}. root names the one BriefBody. The elements form one tree: each used once, at most 6 levels and 32 components, at most 64000 bytes of compact JSON. Only BriefBody, Group and Columns have children. In each component's props, ? marks an optional prop, [a-b] an array's item count, ≤n a string's longest length in characters and ="a"|"b" the only values a prop takes. Components:
- BriefBody {}: The root of every section body; no props, children only. Children: at most 32.
- Group {title?≤160, tone?="plain"|"accent"|"muted"}: A group of components with an optional title. tone accent or muted tints its background, e.g. for a summary across the top. Children: at most 24.
- Columns {widths?[2-4](integer)}: Lays out its children side by side, each child one column (usually a Group). widths gives their relative widths, e.g. [2, 1]; equal without it. A narrow window stacks the columns in the order given. Children: 2-4, one per column.
- Markdown {text≤64000}: GitHub-flavoured Markdown: paragraphs, lists, links, tables and fenced code or log excerpts. Raw HTML is not supported.
- Math {tex≤4000, display?}: A KaTeX formula; display:true sets it on its own line.
- Checklist {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, text≤1000, done}}: Items with done flags.
- Plan {title?≤160, steps[1-30]{id, text≤1000, state="todo"|"doing"|"done"|"blocked"}}: Ordered steps, each todo, doing, done or blocked.
- Findings {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, source≤160, severity="info"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|"critical", text≤2000}}: Review or analysis findings, each with its source (file, tool or reviewer) and severity.
- Metrics {items[1-12]{label≤160, value, unit?≤30, previous?, detail?≤2000}}: Key numbers with optional unit; give previous (the value in your last version) to show the change when both are numbers.
- Table {id, title?≤160, columns[1-12]{key, label≤160}, rows[≤200]{id, cells{<key>: string≤500|number|boolean|null}, sourceIds?[≤12](string)}, selectable?}: A searchable sortable table; every row has a cell for every column key. title defaults to "Table".
- LiveRefs {items[1-50]{kind="task"|"pr"|"ci"|"job"|"review"|"agent"|"machine", id, label?≤160}}: References that Yuzuno shows with their current state: task (e.g. T-12), pr (owner/repo#12), ci (run id), job, review (review id), agent or machine id.
- Attachments {items[1-12]{name, caption?≤500}}: Shows this section's attachments by name with optional captions.
- Sources {items[≤30]{id, label≤160, href≤2000}}: Explicit HTTPS or local file references; Table rows cite them by id in sourceIds.
- LineChart, BarChart, ScatterChart: see charts.
Table and chart ids, row ids, item ids and column keys are unique. Sources hrefs are http(s) URLs or local file paths (optionally :line); Table rows cite them by id in sourceIds.
LiveRefs show Core's records, read each time Home reads the Brief and never saved in your section: your label names the item, and its state is the record's own (a task's board state, a Job's run state), not whether an Agent is working on it now. An item Core does not know shows as not found: check its id. One Core could not read just then shows as couldn't read: leave it, a later read shows its state again. A state you write in Plan, Table, Metrics or Markdown is your account as of when you wrote it (a status's asOf), not live: for the current state of a task, PR, CI run or Job, reference it, as the overview example does with its Job.
Form follows the information, unless the user or Project prefers another: a real screenshot or a labelled sketch (say which) for a UI or layout change, a chart of measured data for quantities and how they relate, a short sentence for a single state. The result, compare and decision examples show each; image shows a screenshot.
Layout: a short answer first, the first Markdown on its own or in a Group with tone accent, since its first paragraph is what a reader sees first; then a Columns of Groups for parts that sit side by side, as in the overview example. Keep each block's id across versions: edit changes one block by its id (see sections).
Advice: an accepted brief_update, or a validateOnly check that passes, may carry up to 3 advice {code, path, reason, guide} on the report and status sections it sent; for an edit, only on the blocks it replaced. They are adjustable hints from lengths and counts (limits.advice), not a score or a limit: nothing is cut, refused or rewritten, the update stays accepted, and a section whose title and captions already say enough may stay as it is. Characters are Unicode code points. Codes:
- long_markdown: A Markdown block over 1200 characters, or a section whose Markdown is over 3000 characters in all.
- summary_may_be_missing: A Table or chart and no non-empty Markdown, Findings or Metrics block.
- duplicate_ref: One LiveRefs or Sources block that names the same target twice.
- many_refs: Over 12 LiveRefs and Sources entries in one section, each target counted once per block.

## charts
- LineChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A line chart from inline points or a data attachment. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
- BarChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A bar chart from inline points or a data attachment; x is usually a label. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
- ScatterChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A scatter plot with numeric x, from inline points or a data attachment. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
Give exactly one of:
- series: inline points [[x, y], ...], at most 500 points across all series. LineChart and BarChart x is a number or a short label; ScatterChart x is a number; y is a number.
- data: {attachment, x, series:[{name, column}]}. attachment names one of this section's attachments whose path ends in .csv, .json or .jsonl (CSV with a header row, a JSON array of objects, or one JSON object per line). x and each column name a CSV header or JSON key. Yuzuno reads the snapshot taken when you wrote the section and downsamples each series to at most 5000 points.
At most 12 series per chart. Use data for anything over 500 points.

## attachments
- attachments [≤12]{name, path?≤4096, url?≤2000, caption?≤500}: Files and links of this section.
- Give exactly one of path or url. name is unique in the section; the body refers to it.
- path: an absolute path on the machine where Core runs. Files up to 25 MB are kept as a snapshot when you write the section; larger files and directories are only referenced and marked "may have changed".
- url: an https link, shown as a link only, never embedded.
Images, data files (CSV, JSON, JSONL), PDF, logs and text (the last 200 lines are previewed) and links. Show them in the body with Attachments; charts read data files (see charts).
Registration alone saves/references a file; it does not show it. Every attachment in a put must be used by a reachable Attachments.items entry with the exact name, or by LineChart/BarChart/ScatterChart data.attachment. Markdown/Sources mentions and disconnected blocks do not count. Multiple components may use the same name. Chart data use does not also display a file preview; add Attachments if that is wanted.
An unused_attachment rejection leaves the old content, snapshots and ask state unchanged. Add a reachable Attachments block, reference a supported data file from a chart, or put the section without the unused registration. Checks use the final merged body, not just an edit's blocks. Existing sections/history remain readable. An unrelated edit keeps already-unused old registrations; removing a previously used attachment's last reference is rejected. A put checks every registration, including old ones.
Image preview example: {"op":"put","key":"preview","kind":"report","title":"Layout preview","attachments":[{"name":"layout.png","path":"/home/me/run/layout.png"}],"body":{"root":"body","elements":{"body":{"type":"BriefBody","props":{},"children":["image"]},"image":{"type":"Attachments","props":{"items":[{"name":"layout.png","caption":"Screenshot of the updated layout"}]}}}}}
Chart-only data example: {"op":"put","key":"training","kind":"status","title":"Training run 12","status":{"asOf":"2026-10-17T08:00:00Z","validFor":3600},"time":{"eta":"2026-10-17T14:00:00Z","nextUpdate":"2026-10-17T09:00:00Z"},"attachments":[{"name":"loss.csv","path":"/home/me/runs/12/loss.csv","caption":"Loss per step"}],"body":{"root":"body","elements":{"body":{"type":"BriefBody","props":{},"children":["metrics","loss"]},"metrics":{"type":"Metrics","props":{"items":[{"label":"Validation loss","value":0.412,"previous":0.437},{"label":"Throughput","value":1830,"unit":"samples/s","previous":1795},{"label":"Step","value":"18k of 40k"}]}},"loss":{"type":"LineChart","props":{"id":"loss","title":"Loss","x":{"label":"Step"},"y":{"label":"Loss"},"data":{"attachment":"loss.csv","x":"step","series":[{"name":"Train","column":"train_loss"},{"name":"Validation","column":"val_loss"}]}}}}}}
Attach what the user should look at: a screenshot or a sketch (its caption says which) and the data file a chart reads. Logs, raw data, full tables and test output are execution evidence: leave them on their Task and link it with LiveRefs instead of attaching them here.

## limits
- Brief: 12 topics, 4 subs per topic, 3 open asks per Agent; seen reports stay 30 days.
- Body: 64000 bytes of compact JSON, 32 components, 6 levels; BriefBody 32 children, Group 24, Columns 2-4.
- Markdown: each fenced code or log block 200 lines. Math: 4000 characters.
- Checklist, Plan and Findings: 30 items each. Metrics: 12. Sources: 30.
- Table: 200 rows, 12 columns.
- Charts: 12 series; inline 500 points in total; data attachments downsampled to 5000 points per series.
- LiveRefs: 50 per section. Attachments: 12 per section; snapshots 25 MB per file, 1 GB per Brief (oldest history pruned first).
- ask: 2-8 options; form 1-8 fields, 2-12 options each.
Over a limit, the rejection says what to keep here and what to leave on the Task.

## errors
A rejected brief_update lists problems {code, path, reason, guide}: at most 5 for each section's format and at most 10 in all. moreProblems says how many more Core found past 10; problems past a section's 5 are not found or counted. path is where in your change (e.g. body.elements.log.props.text); reason says what to change; guide names the brief_guide part to read. Fix them all and call brief_update again with a new requestId.
- invalid_section: The change is not an object.
- unknown_field: A field the format does not have.
- missing_field: A required field is missing.
- invalid_field: A value of the wrong type, format or range.
- invalid_key: The key is not topic or topic/sub.
- unknown_component: A component type outside the catalog.
- too_many: A list over its limit.
- too_long: A text over its limit.
- too_large: The body is over 64000 bytes of compact JSON.
- block_too_long: A Markdown code or log block is over 200 lines.
- too_many_points: An inline chart has over 500 points.
- too_many_refs: The section has over 50 LiveRefs.
- ask_required: kind ask without ask.
- ask_without_reply: An ask without options, freeText, form or choice.
- status_required: kind status without status.
- misplaced_field: ask or status on a section of another kind.
- root: The root is not a BriefBody.
- component_count: Fewer than 1 or more than 32 components.
- not_a_tree: Elements are shared, cyclic or deeper than 6 levels.
- missing_component: A child names a missing element.
- extra_root: More than one BriefBody.
- unused_component: An element not reachable from the root.
- columns_widths: Columns widths that do not match its children.
- duplicate_id: Two items, rows, columns, series or components share an id.
- row_mismatch: A Table row's cells do not match its columns.
- invalid_source: A Sources href that is not an http(s) URL or local path, or a duplicate source id.
- missing_source: A sourceIds entry with no matching source.
- chart_data: A chart without exactly one of series or data.
- missing_attachment: A name not in the section's attachments.
- unused_attachment: An attachment not used by a reachable Attachments block or chart data; add a reference or remove its registration with put.
- chart_attachment: A chart attachment that is not a CSV, JSON or JSONL file with a path.
- attachment_location: An attachment without exactly one of path or url, or with a path that is not absolute or a url that is not https.
- duplicate_attachment: Two attachments share a name.
- ask_only: Your current Project permission allows only your own valid asks and optional noChange. Only the user can select content editors. Read brief_get you.capabilities and keep internal progress in tasks and mail.
Core also rejects version_conflict (a section you change was written after the version you read, or expectedVersion is ahead of the Brief; other sections' writes don't count; the rejection includes latest: merge and retry), no_active_turn (call it during your turn), unknown_element and edit_root (an edit naming a block the section does not have, or its root), and changes that break owner, topic or open-ask rules.

## examples
Each is one change for brief_update changes.

guideParts.sections:
## sections
This guide is the format. What to write and in which form is yuzuno_guide topic brief ("Write for Home"): one conclusion first, important limits beside it, each fact in one place, and execution evidence (logs, raw data, full test output, run and PR lists) left on its Task and linked.
What goes where: Home: a lasting finding, decision or stage result goes in a short report linked to its Task and sources; a current state in a status; a choice for the user in an ask. result_publish shows only in this turn. How to write it: yuzuno_guide brief. Update a section when something changed, not every turn; a status past its validFor shows as stale until new facts refresh it. Details stay on the Task and its sources.
Home content editors are set by the user per Project. brief_get returns you.capabilities. When editContent is false and writeOwnAsk is true, only create/update/resolve/remove your own Asks or send noChange; do not claim sections, convert regular content into an Ask, or write reports/status. When writeOwnAsk is false, this Brief is read-only, including no noChange writes. Ownership rules still apply to editors. Hidden old content remains in team details/history.
brief_update takes changes: [...]. put creates or replaces one section you own:
- put {op:"put", key, kind: ask|report|status, title, body{…}, ask?{…}, status?{…}, time?{…}, attachments?[≤12]{…}}
- key: topic or topic/sub; each part 1-48 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit (round-12, round-12/review). A Brief has at most 12 topics with 4 subs each.
- kind: ask (a question for the user, see ask); report (a result the user reads and marks seen; seen reports stay in history 30 days); status (current state; needs status {asOf, validFor}, validFor 60-31536000 seconds; greyed once asOf + validFor has passed).
- title: 1-120 characters. body: {root, elements}, see content. time: due, eta and nextUpdate, ISO 8601 with a time zone. attachments: see attachments.
edit {op:"edit", key, elements:{<id>: {type, props, children?}}, status?} replaces blocks of a section you own by id and keeps the rest as it was: the other blocks and their order, title, attachments, time and the ask's state. Each id is one the body already has, or a new block named as a child by a block you edit; the root is not edited (rearrange with put). Core checks the whole section again. status (kind status only) refreshes asOf. Day to day, edit the blocks that changed, e.g. {op:"edit", key:"overview", elements:{progress:{type:"Plan", props:{steps:[...]}}}}; put a section to create it or change its layout.
Other changes: {op:"resolve", key} resolves your ask; {op:"remove", key} removes your section (reports and status go to history); {op:"claim", key} takes an orphaned section of your Project; change it in a later brief_update, not in the one that claims it.
Only a section's owner changes it. To add to another Agent's section, put your own section under its key as topic/sub; Home shows them together with each author.
Pass expectedVersion from brief_get. On version_conflict the rejection includes latest: merge and retry with a new requestId. Nothing requires an update each turn; noChange:true is still accepted and changes nothing.
validateOnly:true pre-checks a brief_update: it runs the checks made before the write, with their problems as the update would give them (and latest), and writes nothing: no requestId kept, no version or space reserved, and it is not your update. Its answer has valid, whether the pre-check passed, and checkedAll, only whether it ran all its steps. Checking stops at the first step with problems, so false means later steps did not run and the problems listed may not be all. Checks made only on writing are outside it: sending the update checks version, Turn and permissions again against the Brief as it is then, and can still be refused, e.g. with snapshot_limit when the Brief's snapshots would exceed their total. Use it for a complex section; an ordinary edit needs no check first.
guideParts.ask:
## ask
kind ask needs ask:
- ask {question, reply{options?[2-8]{id, label}, freeText?: true|{prompt?}, form?{…}, choice?{a{id, label, detail?}, b{id, label, detail?}}}}: a question and how the user can answer.
- question: 1-500 characters. reply needs at least one of options, freeText, form or choice; otherwise the change is rejected.
- options: 2-8 buttons; each sends one prefilled reply message to you. freeText: true, or {prompt} to label the text box. choice: two approaches a and b.
- form {id, title≤160, description?≤1000, fields[1-8]{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="text", placeholder?≤160, default?{value≤2000, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="single", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="multi", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value[≤12](string), source≤160}}}: One bounded form: id, title, optional description and 1-8 fields. Each field has id, type (text/single/multi), label, required and optional description. Text may have placeholder. Choices have 2-12 options with stable id, label and optional description. An optional default is {value, source}: source says where it came from; value is text, one option id or an array of option ids. Users explicitly submit answers once to this original conversation; never use forms as native permission approval. At most 8 fields, 12 options each.
Use options for one choice and a form for several related answers, as in the decision and form examples.
The user's answer reaches you as an ordinary message quoting the section. The ask then shows "replied": it leaves Needs you, and brief_get lists it in you.repliedAsks (key, title, repliedAt, the reply in short, updatedSinceReply). It stays until you resolve it with {op:"resolve", key}; nothing closes it for you.
When to resolve: a preference or information you asked for, once you have taken it in; an action the reply authorizes, only after that action is confirmed done and its result is on the existing Task or a Brief section. A green CI or a whole Task being done is not that action. While it runs, or after it fails, keep the ask replied and report progress on the Task or Brief: edit keeps it replied, while put asks it again. Ask again only when the user has something new to decide. A reply executes nothing by itself: act on what the user has authorized, an explicit reply included, without asking for it again, and never infer a retry, merge or wider permission from an answer that does not grant it.
openAsks counts your unresolved asks, open or replied; at most 3 per Agent.
Answers never execute actions: nothing in a Brief merges, deploys or approves; Core approvals stay separate.
guideParts.content:
## content
body is {root, elements}: elements maps ids (a letter, then letters, digits, - or _) to {type, props, children?}. root names the one BriefBody. The elements form one tree: each used once, at most 6 levels and 32 components, at most 64000 bytes of compact JSON. Only BriefBody, Group and Columns have children. In each component's props, ? marks an optional prop, [a-b] an array's item count, ≤n a string's longest length in characters and ="a"|"b" the only values a prop takes. Components:
- BriefBody {}: The root of every section body; no props, children only. Children: at most 32.
- Group {title?≤160, tone?="plain"|"accent"|"muted"}: A group of components with an optional title. tone accent or muted tints its background, e.g. for a summary across the top. Children: at most 24.
- Columns {widths?[2-4](integer)}: Lays out its children side by side, each child one column (usually a Group). widths gives their relative widths, e.g. [2, 1]; equal without it. A narrow window stacks the columns in the order given. Children: 2-4, one per column.
- Markdown {text≤64000}: GitHub-flavoured Markdown: paragraphs, lists, links, tables and fenced code or log excerpts. Raw HTML is not supported.
- Math {tex≤4000, display?}: A KaTeX formula; display:true sets it on its own line.
- Checklist {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, text≤1000, done}}: Items with done flags.
- Plan {title?≤160, steps[1-30]{id, text≤1000, state="todo"|"doing"|"done"|"blocked"}}: Ordered steps, each todo, doing, done or blocked.
- Findings {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, source≤160, severity="info"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|"critical", text≤2000}}: Review or analysis findings, each with its source (file, tool or reviewer) and severity.
- Metrics {items[1-12]{label≤160, value, unit?≤30, previous?, detail?≤2000}}: Key numbers with optional unit; give previous (the value in your last version) to show the change when both are numbers.
- Table {id, title?≤160, columns[1-12]{key, label≤160}, rows[≤200]{id, cells{<key>: string≤500|number|boolean|null}, sourceIds?[≤12](string)}, selectable?}: A searchable sortable table; every row has a cell for every column key. title defaults to "Table".
- LiveRefs {items[1-50]{kind="task"|"pr"|"ci"|"job"|"review"|"agent"|"machine", id, label?≤160}}: References that Yuzuno shows with their current state: task (e.g. T-12), pr (owner/repo#12), ci (run id), job, review (review id), agent or machine id.
- Attachments {items[1-12]{name, caption?≤500}}: Shows this section's attachments by name with optional captions.
- Sources {items[≤30]{id, label≤160, href≤2000}}: Explicit HTTPS or local file references; Table rows cite them by id in sourceIds.
- LineChart, BarChart, ScatterChart: see charts.
Table and chart ids, row ids, item ids and column keys are unique. Sources hrefs are http(s) URLs or local file paths (optionally :line); Table rows cite them by id in sourceIds.
LiveRefs show Core's records, read each time Home reads the Brief and never saved in your section: your label names the item, and its state is the record's own (a task's board state, a Job's run state), not whether an Agent is working on it now. An item Core does not know shows as not found: check its id. One Core could not read just then shows as couldn't read: leave it, a later read shows its state again. A state you write in Plan, Table, Metrics or Markdown is your account as of when you wrote it (a status's asOf), not live: for the current state of a task, PR, CI run or Job, reference it, as the overview example does with its Job.
Form follows the information, unless the user or Project prefers another: a real screenshot or a labelled sketch (say which) for a UI or layout change, a chart of measured data for quantities and how they relate, a short sentence for a single state. The result, compare and decision examples show each; image shows a screenshot.
Layout: a short answer first, the first Markdown on its own or in a Group with tone accent, since its first paragraph is what a reader sees first; then a Columns of Groups for parts that sit side by side, as in the overview example. Keep each block's id across versions: edit changes one block by its id (see sections).
Advice: an accepted brief_update, or a validateOnly check that passes, may carry up to 3 advice {code, path, reason, guide} on the report and status sections it sent; for an edit, only on the blocks it replaced. They are adjustable hints from lengths and counts (limits.advice), not a score or a limit: nothing is cut, refused or rewritten, the update stays accepted, and a section whose title and captions already say enough may stay as it is. Characters are Unicode code points. Codes:
- long_markdown: A Markdown block over 1200 characters, or a section whose Markdown is over 3000 characters in all.
- summary_may_be_missing: A Table or chart and no non-empty Markdown, Findings or Metrics block.
- duplicate_ref: One LiveRefs or Sources block that names the same target twice.
- many_refs: Over 12 LiveRefs and Sources entries in one section, each target counted once per block.
guideParts.charts:
## charts
- LineChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A line chart from inline points or a data attachment. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
- BarChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A bar chart from inline points or a data attachment; x is usually a label. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
- ScatterChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A scatter plot with numeric x, from inline points or a data attachment. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
Give exactly one of:
- series: inline points [[x, y], ...], at most 500 points across all series. LineChart and BarChart x is a number or a short label; ScatterChart x is a number; y is a number.
- data: {attachment, x, series:[{name, column}]}. attachment names one of this section's attachments whose path ends in .csv, .json or .jsonl (CSV with a header row, a JSON array of objects, or one JSON object per line). x and each column name a CSV header or JSON key. Yuzuno reads the snapshot taken when you wrote the section and downsamples each series to at most 5000 points.
At most 12 series per chart. Use data for anything over 500 points.

## attachments
- attachments [≤12]{name, path?≤4096, url?≤2000, caption?≤500}: Files and links of this section.
- Give exactly one of path or url. name is unique in the section; the body refers to it.
- path: an absolute path on the machine where Core runs. Files up to 25 MB are kept as a snapshot when you write the section; larger files and directories are only referenced and marked "may have changed".
- url: an https link, shown as a link only, never embedded.
Images, data files (CSV, JSON, JSONL), PDF, logs and text (the last 200 lines are previewed) and links. Show them in the body with Attachments; charts read data files (see charts).
Registration alone saves/references a file; it does not show it. Every attachment in a put must be used by a reachable Attachments.items entry with the exact name, or by LineChart/BarChart/ScatterChart data.attachment. Markdown/Sources mentions and disconnected blocks do not count. Multiple components may use the same name. Chart data use does not also display a file preview; add Attachments if that is wanted.
An unused_attachment rejection leaves the old content, snapshots and ask state unchanged. Add a reachable Attachments block, reference a supported data file from a chart, or put the section without the unused registration. Checks use the final merged body, not just an edit's blocks. Existing sections/history remain readable. An unrelated edit keeps already-unused old registrations; removing a previously used attachment's last reference is rejected. A put checks every registration, including old ones.

guideParts.limits:
## limits
- Brief: 12 topics, 4 subs per topic, 3 open asks per Agent; seen reports stay 30 days.
- Body: 64000 bytes of compact JSON, 32 components, 6 levels; BriefBody 32 children, Group 24, Columns 2-4.
- Markdown: each fenced code or log block 200 lines. Math: 4000 characters.
- Checklist, Plan and Findings: 30 items each. Metrics: 12. Sources: 30.
- Table: 200 rows, 12 columns.
- Charts: 12 series; inline 500 points in total; data attachments downsampled to 5000 points per series.
- LiveRefs: 50 per section. Attachments: 12 per section; snapshots 25 MB per file, 1 GB per Brief (oldest history pruned first).
- ask: 2-8 options; form 1-8 fields, 2-12 options each.
Over a limit, the rejection says what to keep here and what to leave on the Task.
guideParts.errors:
## errors
A rejected brief_update lists problems {code, path, reason, guide}: at most 5 for each section's format and at most 10 in all. moreProblems says how many more Core found past 10; problems past a section's 5 are not found or counted. path is where in your change (e.g. body.elements.log.props.text); reason says what to change; guide names the brief_guide part to read. Fix them all and call brief_update again with a new requestId.
- invalid_section: The change is not an object.
- unknown_field: A field the format does not have.
- missing_field: A required field is missing.
- invalid_field: A value of the wrong type, format or range.
- invalid_key: The key is not topic or topic/sub.
- unknown_component: A component type outside the catalog.
- too_many: A list over its limit.
- too_long: A text over its limit.
- too_large: The body is over 64000 bytes of compact JSON.
- block_too_long: A Markdown code or log block is over 200 lines.
- too_many_points: An inline chart has over 500 points.
- too_many_refs: The section has over 50 LiveRefs.
- ask_required: kind ask without ask.
- ask_without_reply: An ask without options, freeText, form or choice.
- status_required: kind status without status.
- misplaced_field: ask or status on a section of another kind.
- root: The root is not a BriefBody.
- component_count: Fewer than 1 or more than 32 components.
- not_a_tree: Elements are shared, cyclic or deeper than 6 levels.
- missing_component: A child names a missing element.
- extra_root: More than one BriefBody.
- unused_component: An element not reachable from the root.
- columns_widths: Columns widths that do not match its children.
- duplicate_id: Two items, rows, columns, series or components share an id.
- row_mismatch: A Table row's cells do not match its columns.
- invalid_source: A Sources href that is not an http(s) URL or local path, or a duplicate source id.
- missing_source: A sourceIds entry with no matching source.
- chart_data: A chart without exactly one of series or data.
- missing_attachment: A name not in the section's attachments.
- unused_attachment: An attachment not used by a reachable Attachments block or chart data; add a reference or remove its registration with put.
- chart_attachment: A chart attachment that is not a CSV, JSON or JSONL file with a path.
- attachment_location: An attachment without exactly one of path or url, or with a path that is not absolute or a url that is not https.
- duplicate_attachment: Two attachments share a name.
- ask_only: Your current Project permission allows only your own valid asks and optional noChange. Only the user can select content editors. Read brief_get you.capabilities and keep internal progress in tasks and mail.
Core also rejects version_conflict (a section you change was written after the version you read, or expectedVersion is ahead of the Brief; other sections' writes don't count; the rejection includes latest: merge and retry), no_active_turn (call it during your turn), unknown_element and edit_root (an edit naming a block the section does not have, or its root), and changes that break owner, topic or open-ask rules.
